# Koushik Kotamraju

> Principal security engineer at Yahoo, on the cloud security team (the Paranoids). Ten years in engineering, nine of them in cloud security on AWS. Owns the AWS security baseline for every engineering team on AWS and builds the AI tooling that runs it: models where they help, deterministic gates where a decision touches access, and a benchmark before any tool is trusted. Open to Principal and Staff security engineering roles and to cloud security management. Portfolio: https://koushik.io

Source: the Ascend master resume, v8, locked 2026-11-05. Every figure below is a public figure. Where a claim has a limit, the limit is stated next to it.

## Current role

Principal Technical Security Engineer, Yahoo, Cloud Security (Oct 2026 to present). Senior Technical Security Engineer on the same team from Feb 2022 to Sep 2026.

## What he owns

**The AWS security baseline.** Took ownership of baseline releases at month three in 2022 and has held it since: decides which controls ship for every engineering team on AWS, when each becomes enforced, and which are merged or retired.

**Detection signatures.** Deploys and maintains 200+ Python detection signatures that monitor the baseline across 1,400+ AWS accounts, covering AWS service controls and IAM. Each failed control becomes a per-resource finding with remediation steps the account owner can act on. Owns their correctness: fixed two controls whose findings never reached the ticketing system for months, and a shared policy-evaluation helper that hid real access along with the false positives it had been masking, then audited the fleet for the same pattern. This is configuration-state detection, not detection and response.

**The high-severity enforcement program.** Designed and launched it for every AWS account owner. A three-tier severity model based on what an attacker gains sets each deadline, the full control-to-tier mapping was published a quarter before enforcement, and declining a fix is a written exception with an expiry. Posture metrics follow detection state, not ticket state, so suppressing a finding cannot improve the chart.

## What he built

**AI-assisted toxic-combination correlation engine.** Identifies toxic combinations in cloud misconfigurations, which carry higher risk than the individual findings: for example, a missing IMDSv2 requirement and an over-privileged IAM role on the same instance form one privilege-escalation path. 15 AWS combinations, defined from documented escalation paths in DataDog's public pathfinding.cloud catalog.

**Security controls over MCP.** Embedded security controls into the security team's MCP server, bringing the AWS, GCP, Kubernetes, and Docker baselines into the context of Claude and other AI engines. Developers shift security left, and the code and infrastructure they build is more secure by default. In evals that mimicked feature work across repositories, Terraform included, Claude identified and fetched the applicable baseline in every trial.

**Attack-research pipeline.** Proposed and built an LLM pipeline that turns new AWS, GCP, Docker, and Kubernetes attack techniques from public bulletins and research blogs into draft baseline controls. A cheap model triages, a stronger one analyzes, and every draft waits for human review. A partner detection team adopted its staged design.

**review-aws-iam-policies.** An IAM analysis tool covering 10 privilege-escalation classes. Pairs deterministic checks with a model pass, tags each finding with its source, and maps paths to pathfinding.cloud (65+ paths, DataDog's catalog). Benchmarked against 32 ground-truth findings in 11 synthetic Terraform fixtures written before the evaluation.

**AI-enabled GCP attack-path analysis.** Analyzes GCP attack-path simulation and toxic combinations from Security Command Center. Proposed and built on Cloud Run, BigQuery, and Terraform to rotate resources through the platform's simulation limit, so simulation covers the full resource set and its results reach resource owners. The AWS side is designed, not built.

**AI-assisted review workspace.** Runs cloud security reviews through a workspace built for a coding assistant (skills, hooks, rules, commands) that assembles each dossier, pulls detected state, walks the control checklist, and drafts findings. Nothing is written until he approves the exact text.

**Suppression advisor.** A deterministic advisory engine for alert-suppression requests: scores each request on four signals, caps confidence so it never reads as certain, and hard-blocks exceptions in categories where none is allowed. Rules over a model, because the decision gates access.

## Reviews and influence

- 100+ cloud security architecture reviews since 2021 across AWS, GCP, and Azure for every business unit. Each objection is tied to a named written control; each accepted risk has an owner and an expiry.
- Co-authored the largest control release in the baseline program's history as one of a small senior group, writing most of it and running its gap analysis.
- Four internal technical talks (2023 to 2025). Taught assistant-driven development to a partner team whose engineers now ship into a platform he owns.

## Research and in progress

- A research pipeline routing work across 19 models from 5 providers: cheap-model triage, a mid-tier evaluation council, and anonymized peer review before synthesis. Full sweeps run from $1.40 on metered pricing.
- In progress: a context correlation engine for security incidents, bringing complete context around an asset's configuration history and how to kill the attack chain, based on AI triage of the incident.

## Earlier

- CYR3CON, Cyber Security Architect and Team Lead, Infrastructure and Security (Dec 2017 to Jan 2022; intern until Apr 2019). Led the infrastructure and security teams, up to 7 engineers: sprint planning, project scope, mentoring. Designed the multi-account AWS foundation as code with no static credentials in the deployment path. Ran on-prem data-center servers, firewalls, and VMs. Deployed a honeypot network for the company's threat-intelligence product.
- Infosys, Systems Engineer (Dec 2015 to May 2017). Automated a US logistics client's partner data exchange on Dell Boomi, raising throughput about 80%.

## Where the depth stops

- Kubernetes: authored controls and reviewed architectures; has not operated a cluster in production.
- Detection: builds posture evaluation, not streaming detection and response, and has not carried a D&R pager.
